analysis.note: Revised per the verifier: morphologically this is the feminine genitive singular of the compound kṣīṇavṛtti, not a neuter genitive; taken formally as ‘of the subsided vṛtti.’ Vyāsa nevertheless construes the sense as applying to the citta/cetas whose pratyaya has subsided.

verification.detail: compound stem kṣīṇavṛtti as Stri/Sasthi/Eka: pass; relation karmadharaya: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Adjectival participial stem agreeing with maṇeḥ; in context, the bhāṣya takes the jewel as a crystal-like illustrative example.
Printed as -eva in sandhi with preceding abhijātasya.
Genitive singular in the simile abhijātasya maṇer iva.

samasa.vigraha: grahītā ca grahaṇaṃ ca grāhyaṃ ca, teṣu

analysis.note: Locative plural sphere of samāpatti; the bhāṣya maps the members to puruṣa, indriya, and bhūta.

verification.detail: compound stem grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhya as Napumsaka/Saptami/Bahu: pass; relation dvandva: unsupported (logged)

samasa.vigraha: tatsthasya tadañjanatā; bhāṣye: teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ

analysis.note: Feminine abstract in -tā. The analysis follows Vyāsa’s semantic vigraha: ‘for what is situated in them, assumption of their form.’ Nested tat-stha = tasmin/teṣu sthita; tad-añjanatā is not literal collyrium-application but taking on that form/color.

verification.detail: compound stem tatsthatadañjanatā as Stri/Prathama/Eka: pass; relation tatpurusa: unsupported (logged)

analysis.note: Predicate nominative: the preceding tatsthatadañjanatā is what is called samāpatti.

justifications.decision: The form is taken morphologically as a feminine genitive singular karmadhāraya, while Vyāsa’s artha-gloss and later mention of cetas determine that the relevant bearer is the mind.
options_considered: A neuter genitive bahuvrīhi agreeing directly with cetas
A non-technical sense such as ‘of diminished conduct’
A feminine genitive compound kṣīṇā vṛttiḥ, commentarially applied to the mind
justifications.chosen: Grammatically, kṣīṇavṛtteḥ is ‘of the subsided vṛtti’; in the sūtra’s commentarial sense, it describes the mind whose vṛtti/pratyaya has subsided.

evidence.translation: ‘kṣīṇavṛtti’ means ‘whose pratyaya has set/subsided’ or ‘of the subsided pratyaya.’
Vyāsa explicitly supplies the referent as ‘of the mind comparable to a fine jewel.’

justifications.decision: The phrase is not an additional doctrinal subject; Vyāsa marks it as a dṛṣṭānta and explains its point through the crystal’s taking on the color/form of its support.
options_considered: Literal social sense: ‘like a well-born jewel’
A mere decorative comparison with no interpretive force
A crystal/jewel simile showing transparent conformity to the support
justifications.chosen: abhijātasya maṇer iva is an illustrative simile of a clear crystal-jewel.

evidence.translation: ‘Like a fine jewel’ is the introduction of an example.

evidence.quote: yathā sphaṭika upāśrayabhedāt tattadrūpoparakta upāśrayarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate tathā grāhyālambanoparaktaṃ cittaṃ grāhyasamāpannaṃ grāhyasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate.
evidence.translation: As a crystal, depending on different supports, is colored by this or that form and appears in the form of the support, so the mind colored by a graspable support appears in the graspable’s own form.

justifications.decision: The compound is taken as a locative plural dvandva naming the possible supports in which the mind’s samāpatti occurs.
options_considered: grahaṇa as only the abstract act of grasping
grahītṛ as any empirical receiver or taker
The Yogic triad puruṣa–indriya–bhūta supplied by Vyāsa
justifications.chosen: grahītṛ-grahaṇa-grāhya denotes the triad: grasper/puruṣa, grasping-instruments/indriyas, and graspable objects/bhūtas.

evidence.translation: Vyāsa glosses ‘in the grasper, grasping, and graspable’ as ‘in puruṣa, senses, and elements.’
In the case of grahaṇas, it is to be understood with respect to the senses too.
When colored by the support that is the grahītṛ-puruṣa, it has entered into the grahītṛ-puruṣa and appears in that form.

justifications.decision: tat-stha is read as ‘situated in them’ and tad-añjanatā as taking on their form/color, not literal smearing or collyrium. The compound relation is represented as tatsthasya tadañjanatā, following Vyāsa’s teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ.
options_considered: Two unrelated properties: merely being there plus being stained
The mind’s taking on the form of the support while situated in it
justifications.chosen: tatsthatadañjanatā is ‘the assumption of their form by what is situated in them.’

evidence.quote: yā tatsthatadañjanatā teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ sā samāpattir ity ucyate.
evidence.translation: That tat-stha-tad-añjanatā is the assumption of that form by what is situated in them; that is called samāpatti.
Colored by a grahaṇa-support and coalesced with grahaṇa, it appears in the form of grahaṇa.

justifications.decision: Vyāsa repeatedly explains samāpatti with samāpanna and svarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate: the mind, colored by a support, appears in that support’s own form. The sūtra’s predicate defines this as samāpatti.
options_considered: samāpatti as the mind’s coalescent assumption of the support’s form
justifications.chosen: samāpatti is rendered as cognitive ‘coalescence’ or engrossed conformity, not as accident or mere meeting.

evidence.translation: The mind, colored by a graspable support and coalesced with the graspable, appears in the graspable’s own form.

translation: For the mind whose fluctuation (vṛtti) has subsided, as with a clear crystal-jewel, coalescence (samāpatti) is its taking on their form while it is situated among the grasper (grahītṛ), the grasping-instruments (grahaṇa), and the graspables (grāhya).
one_shot_delta: A commentary-blind translation might take abhijāta maṇi as just ‘well-born jewel,’ missing Vyāsa’s crystal example and the color/form-taking function of the simile.
It might render grahaṇa as only ‘grasping’ in the abstract, whereas Vyāsa identifies grahaṇas here with the senses and the full triad with puruṣa, indriyas, and bhūtas.
It might read tadañjana literally as ‘smearing/applying collyrium,’ rather than as the mind’s assumption of the form of the object in which it is situated.
It might fail to supply citta/cetas for kṣīṇavṛtteḥ and thus miss that the sūtra describes the mind whose pratyayas have subsided.
analyzer_disagreements: ByT5 split kṣīṇa_vṛtteḥ and analysed only vṛtteḥ as SGM; I analyse kṣīṇavṛtteḥ as one feminine genitive singular karmadhāraya compound, because the text and bhāṣya treat kṣīṇavṛtti as a semantic unit. This revision avoids the rejected neuter-genitive claim, for which the verifier derived kṣīṇavṛttinaḥ.
ByT5 gave abhijātasya with lemma abhijan; I use the nominal participial stem abhijāta, masculine genitive singular, agreeing with maṇeḥ.
ByT5 treated grahītṛ and grahaṇa as Cp elements with grāhyeṣu as the inflected item; I record the whole locative plural dvandva compound stem grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhya.

ByT5 segmented tad_stha_tad_añjana_tā; I analyse tatsthatadañjanatā as a single feminine abstract noun with compound structure, since the bhāṣya glosses the whole expression as teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ.
mula: kṣīṇavṛtter abhijātasyeva maṇer grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu tatsthatadañjanatā samāpattiḥ
commentary_lines: yathā sphaṭika upāśrayabhedāt tattadrūpoparakta upāśrayarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate tathā grāhyālambanoparaktaṃ cittaṃ grāhyasamāpannaṃ grāhyasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsate.
tathā muktapuruṣālambanoparaktaṃ muktapuruṣasamāpannaṃ muktapuruṣasvarūpākāreṇa nirbhāsata iti.
tad evam abhijātamaṇikalpasya cetaso grahītṛgrahaṇagrāhyeṣu puruṣendriyabhūteṣu yā tatsthatadañjanatā teṣu sthitasya tadākārāpattiḥ sā samāpattir ity ucyate.
